classification.difficultyReason: Essentially the same as p32-q18: find the apex time, substitute for the greatest height, solve for sinα, then take an inverse sine. Part a adds a decimal answer and part b gives an exact value.

content.prompt: A ball is projected from ground level at angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal. Take $g=10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The initial speed is $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and the greatest height is $20\text{ m}$. Find $\alpha$ to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
At the greatest height, $\dot y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}\dot y&=30\sin\alpha-10t\\0&=30\sin\alpha-10t\\t&=3\sin\alpha\end{align*}$$The height at this time is $20\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=-5t^2+30t\sin\alpha\\20&=-5(3\sin\alpha)^2+30\sin\alpha(3\sin\alpha)\\20&=-45\sin^2\alpha+90\sin^2\alpha\\\sin^2\alpha&=\frac49\\\sin\alpha&=\frac23\\\alpha&\approx42^\circ\end{align*}$$The angle of projection is acute.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The initial speed is $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and the greatest height is $15\text{ m}$. Find $\alpha$ exactly.

answer.worked:
At the greatest height, $\dot y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}\dot y&=20\sin\alpha-10t\\0&=20\sin\alpha-10t\\t&=2\sin\alpha\end{align*}$$The height at this time is $15\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=-5t^2+20t\sin\alpha\\15&=-5(2\sin\alpha)^2+20\sin\alpha(2\sin\alpha)\\15&=-20\sin^2\alpha+40\sin^2\alpha\\\sin^2\alpha&=\frac34\\\sin\alpha&=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\\alpha&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$The angle of projection is acute.
